offence_severity: Life imprisonment / 10 years rigorous imprisonment / 1 year imprisonment
physical_harm: Death of 1 1/2 year old daughter and injuries to wife and mother
number_of_offences: Charged under 342, 307 (2 counts), 302; upheld under 302, 307 (1 count), 342
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the prosecution's case that the appellant assaulted his wife and mother with a sharp edged weapon, caused the death of his daughter, and wrongfully confined his wife and mother within the house. The court also accepted the evidence of the injuries sustained by the wife and mother, the post-mortem report of the daughter, and the testimonies of the medical experts.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly PW2 (the wife), as credible and reliable, noting that she not only suffered the assault but survived to provide detailed accounts. The court also found PW1 and PW8 to be supportive of PW2's version. PW3's credibility was undermined due to her hostile testimony and attempt to attribute her injuries to a fall.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court not stated
investigation_status: Charge-sheet was filed against the appellant for offences punishable under Sections 342, 307 (2 counts) and 302 IPC
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted and sentenced; High Court: Upheld conviction and sentence; Supreme Court: Modified conviction and reduced sentence
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant picked up a quarrel with his wife, assaulted her with a sharp edged weapon, and when his mother intervened to save his wife, she too was assaulted. The ruckus caused by the quarrel and assault woke up the 1 1/2 year old daughter, who started crying, and the appellant went inside the room and hit her, causing her death. The appellant then wrongfully confined his wife and mother within the house.
defence_argument: The appellant's counsel argued that the material on record sufficiently proved that he was a person of unsound mind, that he had been treated by a Psychiatrist and was taking medicines for his illness, that the writings on the walls of the appellant's house suggested he was mentally unsound, and that his conduct after the event was suggestive of his being of unsound mind.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the principle that the burden of proving the existence of circumstances that would bring the case within the purview of Section 84 of the IPC lies squarely upon the person claiming the benefit of that provision. The standard of proof for discharge of the burden is not the same as that expected of the prosecution.
precedent_relied_upon: Dahyabhai Chhaganbhai Thakkar v. State of Gujarat (1964) 7 SCR 361; State of U.P. v. Ram Swarup and Anr. (1974) 4 sec 764: 1975 (1) SCR 409; Bhikari v. State of Uttar Pradesh AIR 1966 SC 1: 1965 SCR 194
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the finding that the appellant committed culpable homicide without premeditation in a sudden fight and in the heat of passion. The Court held that the appellant did not act in a cruel or unusual manner and did not take an undue advantage. The conviction under Section 302 was not justified, and the sentence was modified to Section 304 Part-II with 10 years rigorous imprisonment.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The Court considered that the appellant was working as a government servant with no history of mental health complaints, and that his wife and mother did not suggest any mental ailment except for sleeplessness, which was attributed to excessive drinking.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The Court considered that the appellant assaulted his wife, mother, and child, and that the assault on the child resulted in fatal injuries, indicating a lack of understanding of the consequences of his actions.
other_sentence_order: The Court affirmed the sentence awarded in default of payment of fine and granted the appellant the benefit of Section 428 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
